title: POIROT: Interrogating Agents for Failure Detection in Multi-Agent Systems (+ BLAME benchmark)

title: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures

No plan/tool/observation cross-component taxonomy; no matched no-op/placebo control against real agent runs. Different manipulated variable and different ground-truth source than B2.1's construction-based, real-trajectory substitution protocol -- not a method-twin.

title: CausalFlow: Causal Attribution and Counterfactual Repair for LLM Agent Failures
why: Freshness-sweep candidate (2026-07-04): confirmed via WebFetch abstract read to compute step-level Causal Responsibility Scores via counterfactual intervention within a single sequential trajectory (no plan/tool/observation cross-component taxonomy), and to propose a new attribution+repair algorithm meant to outperform heuristic refinement (an outcome-tier method paper), not a benchmark/protocol for validating other methods against manufactured ground truth. Different manipulated variable and different paper archetype than B2.1 -- not a method-twin.

title: Who&When Pro: Can LLMs Really Attribute Failures in AI Agents?
why: Scoop-check nearest neighbor (2026-08-15, portfolio ZB2.1 review; verified via arXiv API this run: v1 published 2026-07-10, Jiale Liu et al.). Constructs 12,326 failed trajectories by replaying a successful prefix and injecting a failure, calling the injected step a 'golden label' -- occupies B2.1's manufacture-forward territory at scale. Partial scoop: no class-matched no-op control, no identity-replay tier, no bypass arm, no per-class flip-rate margin, no measurement of the substitution premise. Cited with concede-and-claim positioning; B2.1's headline shifts to the certification-validity claim (RQ2/RQ3 + certification-rejection rate).
authors_bib: Jiale Liu and Huajun Xi and Shaokun Zhang and Yifan Zeng and Tianwei Yue and Chi Wang and Jian Kang and Qingyun Wu and Huazheng Wang
